hypothesis: Replacing the per-byte string-body scan (L247-251) with a dedicated inner loop that consumes backslash-escaped pairs should improve throughput by 30-40% because 75% of fixture bytes are inside strings and the tight loop removes four per-byte tests.

steps.change: Replace the `line % interval === 0` modulo check at L271 and L306 with a `nextCp` counter. Initialize `let nextCp = 0;` after L224, and replace the two modulo checks with `if (line === nextCp)` followed by `nextCp += interval` inside the checkpoint push block.

Extract the string-body scanning logic from the `if (inString)` block (L247-251) into a dedicated inner loop. When entering a string (`case 0x22` at L254-256, after `inString = true`), immediately jump to a tight loop: `while (i < n) { const b = buf[i++]; if (b === 0x22) { inString = false; break; } if (b === 0x5c) { if (i < n) i++; else { escaped = true; break; } } }`. Remove the original `if (inString)` block since strings are now consumed by the inner loop.

Handle the `escaped` flag carry-over at the top of the per-chunk loop (before the `for (let i = 0; i < n; i++)` at L245). Add: `if (escaped) { escaped = false; if (inString && i < n) i++; }`. This ensures a dangling backslash at a chunk boundary correctly escapes the first byte of the next chunk.

Adjust the outer loop's `for (let i = 0; i < n; i++)` increment to account for the inner string loop already advancing `i`. Change `for (let i = 0; i < n; i++)` to `for (let i = 0; i < n; )` and add explicit `i++` in each `switch` case and the default branch, except after the inner string loop (which already advanced `i`).

expected_outcome.rationale: The research brief measured the tight string-skip loop at 1.498 vs 1.130 for per-byte handling (+33%). Combined with the nextCp counter (1-3% additional gain), the total should reach 30-40%. The fixture spends 75% of bytes inside strings (avg 26.2 B per string), so removing four per-byte tests (inString, escaped, 0x5c, 0x22) and replacing them with a two-test inner loop should cut per-byte cost significantly.

critic_review.rejection_reason: H001: The stated hypothesis covers only the tight string-body inner loop, but step 1 adds an independent change (a nextCp counter replacing the line % interval modulo), and expected_outcome folds that 1-3% into the 30-40% estimate. Two interventions would be measured as one result. Fix: drop step 1 and re-estimate impact for the string loop alone.
